label: reproductive
interpretation: Reproductive outcomes are studied in just 40 papers (8%), despite evidence that PM2.5 exposure during pregnancy is associated with preterm birth and impaired fetal development. Gap Score: 0.77.

label: neurological
interpretation: Neurological outcomes appear in only 42 of 502 health papers (8%), despite strong biological plausibility (PM2.5→neuroinflammation→cognitive decline). Gap Score: 0.74.

label: mental_health
interpretation: Mental health outcomes appear in 96 papers (19%). Post-wildfire PTSD, depression, and ecological grief represent a growing burden that the literature is only beginning to address. Gap Score: 0.53.

label: homeless
interpretation: Unhoused populations appear in only 6 papers (1%), yet face near-total exposure (no shelter, no evacuation) and zero adaptive capacity. Gap Score: 0.90.

label: indigenous
interpretation: Indigenous communities appear in 35 papers (7%). Their disproportionate exposure (land-based livelihoods, remote locations) and compounded social vulnerabilities make this the field's most critical equity gap. Gap Score: 0.64.

label: racial_minorities
interpretation: Racial and ethnic minorities appear in 30 papers (6%), despite strong evidence of environmental health inequities. Gap Score: 0.61.

label: bio_vs_social_imbalance
interpretation: Biological mechanisms are mentioned 0.7× more often than social determinants (829 vs 1180 mentions). This asymmetry suggests the field systematically undertheorises social pathways — limiting the design of equity-focused interventions.
